clue.text: Gasp about restriction, though compliant enough

indicators.note: the word for gasping is placed around the restriction, enclosing it

parts.note: to gasp is to pant for breath
a tie is something that restricts or binds you

explanation.surface: Someone gasping against a restraint is nonetheless being fairly cooperative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PANT around TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient person puts up with things without complaint, so is sufficiently accommodating.

clue.text: The new wife happily going into prison

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
things that go happily go well

explanation.surface: A newly married woman is cheerfully going off to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' is a link here, not a container. Bridewell was a London house of correction, whose name became a general word for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, after the London institution of that name, became an old general term for a jail or lock-up.

clue.text: Music-writing family

explanation.surface: A family of composers is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses: a tune, a style or tone of expression in words, and a line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of melody, a particular tone in speech or prose, and a lineage or breed.

clue.text: Inertia in operation

explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is idleness or lack of movement; read as two words, 'in action' means working or operating.

clue.text: Breaking down pretence ended in mutual support

indicators.note: the words are broken up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Once someone's pretence collapsed, the result was people relying on one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' shuffles PRETENCE ENDED IN, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Interdependence means each party relying on the other, which is support given both ways.

clue.text: There's nothing left, it's agreed

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: if everything is RIGHT, then nothing is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as words, 'all right' means every part is on the right side, none left; as a phrase it signals assent, like 'OK'.

clue.text: Trunk or boot or some other name for a container

indicators.note: the phrase 'boot or some' acts as a container, holding the required letters inside it

explanation.surface: A list of names for luggage: trunk, boot, or something else that holds things.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'booT OR SOme'. 'Trunk', 'boot' and 'container' all look like luggage, but the definition is the body sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the human body without head or limbs, the anatomical torso.

clue.text: Superficial yet striking party

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a side is one party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: A party on strike is taking only a shallow view.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside as an adjective means external or on the surface, so shallow.

clue.text: Vegetable bed absorbing a bishop

indicators.note: the bed takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A garden bed of vegetables has swallowed up a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts A and RR inside COT. 'bed' looks like a garden bed; it is a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: The carrot is an orange root vegetable.

clue.text: Allow for real change in the betting system

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the betting system

parts.note: the Tote is the totalisator, a pool betting system at British racecourses

indicators.note: the letters of real are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Gamblers allow for a genuine shake-up in how bets are run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' makes LERA from REAL, and 'in' puts it inside TOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to put up with or permit something.

clue.text: Where chirpy creatures may well be seen behind bars

definitions.text: Where chirpy creatures may well be seen behind bars

parts.words: Where chirpy creatures may well be seen behind bars
parts.note: behind bars suggests prisoners, but the chirpy creatures are songbirds kept in a wire enclosure

explanation.surface: Cheerful folk might well end up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage with bars where pet songbirds that chirp are kept.

clue.text: Putting press in charge is incongruous

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Putting the newspapers in control is an odd idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests newspapers, but it is the laundry sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ironic is at odds with what was expected, so out of keeping.

clue.text: Object about the thread being twisted

indicators.note: the word for object goes around the thread

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
twine is strong thread or string

explanation.surface: Something tangled in thread is getting twisted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts END around TWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Entwined means wound round one another, coiled together.

clue.text: The elder representing the monarch in years gone by

definitions.text: the monarch in years gone by

indicators.note: the letters of 'The elder' are rearranged to represent something new

explanation.surface: An older man stands in for a king of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representing' rearranges THE ELDER. Ethelred was an Anglo-Saxon king of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an English king before the Norman conquest.

clue.text: No high-rise accommodation for him!

parts.note: reads as a person who refuses to live in tower blocks, but it means someone from flat country

explanation.surface: Someone who won't live in a tower block.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowlanders, Scotland's southern lowland people, live where the land does not rise high.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from low-lying country, not the hills or mountains.

clue.text: Trainers managed to keep within bounds

indicators.note: the letters of the word are handled and arranged anew

explanation.surface: Coaches succeeded in keeping things under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges TRAINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or control, limiting what something does.

clue.text: A sweet but bovine look

explanation.definitionFit: A bull's-eye is a hard round striped mint, and literally the gaze of a male cow.

clue.text: Uninformed French article about a certain contention

indicators.note: the French article goes around the other pieces

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article
a war is a particular conflict or contention

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece on some dispute is ill-informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A WAR inside UNE. 'article' looks like a piece of writing; it is the grammatical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means without knowledge of something, so not told.

clue.text: In time coming to accept one is not permanent

indicators.note: the period of time takes in the letter for one

parts.note: a term is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In time one comes round to accepting that nothing lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts I inside TERM after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is provisional, holding only until something lasting replaces it.

clue.text: Catching without cash so provoking!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the catching word surrounds the cash

parts.note: netting fish is catching them
L is the abbreviation for a pound, standing for cash

explanation.surface: Being caught short of money is really annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: NETTING goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettling means irritating or annoying someone, like the sting of the plant.

clue.text: Stagger the salvage collector

explanation.walkthrough: A totter, in Britain, is a rag-and-bone man who collects scrap from rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk unsteadily; a totter is also British slang for a scavenger who gathers discarded goods.

clue.text: Robber given a small coin and content

indicators.note: the word and becomes the contents of the coin word

parts.note: a bit is an old term for a small coin

explanation.surface: A thief is handed a small coin and is satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like 'satisfied' but signals that AND is contained in BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber, especially an outlaw on the roads.

clue.text: A wild animal doing badly

indicators.note: the word doing is done badly, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wild beast is faring poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DOING.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Stretched out once served

parts.note: ex means former, once
to tend customers is to serve them

explanation.surface: Someone who has served in the past is now lying at full length.
explanation.definitionFit: Extended means lengthened or spread to full reach.

clue.text: Declare a man in it to be in the wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put in the wrong order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists a man involved in the affair is at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in the wrong' rearranges A MAN IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it firmly.

clue.text: Only half of them returned call, and that's sickening

indicators.note: only the second half of the word them is used
the word for call is read backwards, returned

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as before a court

explanation.surface: A returned phone call from half of the group made someone feel ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half of' takes EM from THEM; 'returned' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic causes vomiting, so it makes you feel sick.

clue.text: Study weight put down

parts.note: a den is a private study room
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A weight in the study has been set down.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, to criticise or disparage.
